democratic.summary: A small, mixed set criticizes concentrated corporate and special-interest power, unequal rules, exploitation, and attacks on workers, while generally seeking fairer markets rather than capitalism's abolition.
democratic.caveat: Only 22 claims appear, and several concern unrelated foreign affairs, child labor, or broad economic description.

republican.summary: Documents praise free enterprise, private-sector innovation, property ownership, and linked economic and political freedom, while condemning Marxism, bureaucracy, government redistribution, and crony capitalism.
republican.caveat: The packet includes foreign-policy ideology and historical description alongside domestic economic positions.

dsa.summary: Documents describe capitalism as exploitative and undemocratic, advocate its abolition or transformation, and propose working-class control, public banking, cooperatives, solidarity economies, and decommodified essentials.
dsa.caveat: Some examples describe interim reforms or organizational strategy rather than a complete post-capitalist design.

democratic_vs_republican.summary: Democratic examples criticize concentrated power and unfair market rules; Republican examples defend free enterprise and private-sector primacy while separately opposing crony capitalism.

democratic_vs_dsa.summary: Democratic examples seek competition, fair rules, and corporate accountability within markets; DSA examples identify capitalism itself as exploitative and advocate democratic economic replacement.

republican_vs_dsa.summary: Republican examples treat private enterprise and ownership as foundations of freedom; DSA examples seek working-class democratic control and abolition of capitalist ownership relations.
